note: The five kinds of audit a provider meets, in plain words, for the audit-day page's glossary (REQ-018 FR-11, AC-4; D-1907). Written by the product owner's research of 14 October 2026 (section B of product/research/webinars/2026-10-14-what-auditors-look-for.md) and checked against the Commission's registration pages for the cycle; NOT NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission text. The verification and certification pathways themselves are in audit-types.json.
author: readyline

items.name: Provisional audit
items.description: Your first registration before you have participants. The auditor checks your documents, forms and credentials; there is nobody to interview yet.

items.name: First audit with participants
items.description: Your first audit once you support people. The auditor reads your documents and your registers, and talks to your workers and some participants.

items.name: Mid-term audit
items.description: For certification only, about 18 months into your three-year registration. It covers governance and operational management and anything that had a corrective action last time.

items.name: Renewal audit
items.description: Before your registration ends, every three years. A full audit again, against the standards that apply to you then.

items.name: Conditional or follow-up audit
items.description: When the Commission sets conditions on your registration, an auditor comes back to check they are met.
